text:
| Layer | Technology | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Language / runtime | Rust 1.98.1, pinned exactly by `rust-toolchain.toml` (rustfmt + clippy); workspace `rust-version = "1.96"`, edition 2024 | One native binary `viola` / `viola.exe`. 1.96 is the declared floor (the security toolchain floor; sysinfo 0.39.6 needs 1.95, std `File::lock` 1.89, rmcp 1.88). CI checks the floor in the `msrv` job: 1.96 is installed by `rustup toolchain install 1.96` and selected with `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.96`, which outranks `rust-toolchain.toml`, so the pin is untouched. The separate `fuzz/` workspace alone builds on `nightly-2026-09-20`, pinned by `fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml` |

subject: stack
text: | Backend framework (concurrency model) | Hybrid: std threads for `run`, `hook`, `send`, `wait` and every other CLI verb; Tokio 1.53.1 built only inside `mcp` | No async runtime on the hot `hook` path. The async ecosystem is used only where rmcp requires it |

subject: stack
text: | CLI parser | clap 4.6.7 (derive; `default-features = false` with `std`, `derive`, `help`, `usage`, `error-context`, `suggestions` — its default set minus `color`, so help and usage output is plain and no colour/terminal crate is in the graph) | Subcommands `run · revive · send · wait · last · list · answer · hook · mcp · verify · pause · release · link · unlink · plugin install` |

subject: stack
text: | PTY layer | portable-pty `=0.8.1` (pinned) behind viola's own `pty` seam; windows-sys 0.61.2 for the `TerminateProcess` kill fallback, the host console's raw/VT modes (`Win32_System_Console`) and its input read (`ReadConsoleW`, behind `viola_pty::host_stdin()`); libc `=0.2.189` (Unix only) for the host tty's raw mode — both behind `HostTerminal`; windows-sys also restricts every `viola` process's DLL search to System32 (`SetDefaultDllDirectories`) and pre-loads the sideloaded `conpty.dll` by absolute path (`LoadLibraryExW`, `Win32_System_LibraryLoader`). On Windows x64 the ConPTY host is Microsoft's `Microsoft.Windows.Console.ConPTY` 1.24.260710001 (`conpty.dll` + `OpenConsole.exe`, MIT), a vendored non-crate binary pair under `vendor/conpty/`, embedded in `viola` | Hosts the unmodified `claude` in the sideloaded ConPTY (Windows x64; the inbox ConPTY is the fail-open fallback and the host on other Windows targets) or openpty (Unix) |

subject: stack
text: | Screen model | vt100 0.16.2 | Pre-send readiness and modal detection on `run`'s feed thread, handed a copy of the pump's output after the human's write, and the screen of `viola verify`'s five interactive probe runs. `run` never reads content; `Screen::rows()` is the only row-text exit, read by `verify` alone for its signature-only `--record` screen fixtures |

subject: stack
text: | Wrapper IPC | interprocess 2.4.4 `local_socket` (sync API; the Tokio flavour, `interprocess/tokio`, only in `viola-channel`'s feature-gated `tokio_client::TokioClient`, used by `viola-mcp` alone, which opens a Windows pipe through the same SQOS + overlapped `client::open_handle`); on Windows the client opens the pipe itself with windows-sys 0.61.2 `CreateFileW(SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT \| SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION \| FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED)` and adopts the handle with `local_socket::Stream::try_from`, never interprocess's default connect. The server's pipe DACL is converted from SDDL by windows-sys (`Win32_Security_Authorization`); on Unix, libc gives the uid for the per-user socket directory and the socket is chmod 0600 after the bind | One endpoint per `viola run`: a named pipe on Windows, a Unix domain socket elsewhere. The Windows open leaves the server able to identify, never impersonate, the client (as measured at chunk 2026-09-25-security-prerequisites; security-plan Decisions Log `2026-09-25`) |

subject: stack
text: | Database | None. ndjson append logs + atomically replaced JSON snapshots on the local filesystem | Authoritative audit trail and mutable state (wheel mirror, links, budget readings) |

subject: stack
text: | ORM / migrations | N/A. Every record carries `v`, readers skip unknown kinds and fields, and a snapshot with an unsupported `v` is rebuilt by replaying the log. The exception is process-log lines (home-level role files and instance detail files): they carry no `v`, and their version lives in the schema filename (`schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json`), because obs's default-deny field list admits no `v` key | Stands in for schema migration |

subject: stack
text: | State-file primitives | tempfile 3.27.0 `persist` through one shared helper (`viola_state::fs::replace_private`: the mode is set on the temp file before the write, then `sync_all` and `persist`) for snapshots and every other replaced file; std `File::lock` on separate `.lock` files, opened for write (Windows refuses an exclusive lock on an append-only handle); std `OpenOptions::append` (one `write` per line); the strict-modes check and private-dir creation through libc (Unix modes and owner) and windows-sys (owner + DACL, and the protected user + SYSTEM DACL on a home created outside the user's profile, `Win32_UI_Shell` `GetUserProfileDirectoryW`; a DACL that cannot be set fails the creation) | Crash-safe multi-process writes with no C code |

subject: stack
text: | Content hash | sha2 `=0.11.0` (`default-features = false`; pure Rust, no `cc`) | SHA-256 of the exe bytes, truncated to the first 8 bytes (16 hex), for the `bin/` and `plugin/` `<version>-<hash>` keys, and to re-hash an existing pinned copy (read in 64 KiB chunks) before every reuse; on Windows x64 also the full SHA-256 of each held ConPTY companion against its compiled pin (`viola_state::pin::pin_companions`). A product dependency of `viola-state`; the root dev-dependency stays for its known-answer test (`tests/contract_content_hash.rs`). `[profile.dev.package.sha2] opt-level = 3`, so dev and test builds hash the debug exe at release speed |
